rationale: Representational correction in the promoted reconstruction fact: its statement said the divergence was observed across three ladders while the same sentence lists four distinct shapes, and it did not cite the five-voter run of the demote/promote ladder. The wording now counts and names the four ladders (no snapshot; snapshot then RemoveServer; snapshot then Promote back; the demote/promote ladder exercised at three and at five voters) and cites the corresponding receipts; the measured values and conditions are unchanged.

knowledge.statement: A restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled over a commit-tracking log store reconstructs a configuration that is not the one recorded in the node's own log whenever the tracked commit index covers that node's last configuration entry, in both directions and across four ladders: the no-snapshot case reported latest_config_index 0 with no servers against a single-voter entry at log index 1; the snapshot-then-remove case reported the snapshot's two voters, one of them the peer removed at log index 103, against the single-voter entry there; the snapshot-then-promote case reported one voter, the promoted peer still carried as a nonvoter, against the two-voter entry at log index 104; and the demote/promote ladder reported one voter against the committed entries of three voters at index 106 and of five voters at the same index. The public GetConfiguration view reported the same value, and the flag-disabled controls and the within-flag case whose configuration entry sits above the replayed prefix all reconstructed the entry's own index and voter count.
knowledge.conditions: NewRaft restart over the same log, stable and snapshot stores; RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore; the node's last configuration entry is either inside the applied prefix replayed from the tracked commit index (divergence, in either direction) or above it (correct reconstruction); no membership change is issued after the restart.
